answer: Trust propagates from authenticated seeds through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so voting weight reflects reachable trust rather than claimed identities. A sybil cluster with small boundary has low conductance—its external edge weight is small relative to its volume—and thus receives little walk flow when seed mass and per-identity influence are bounded. Min-cut and transitivity bounds quantify leakage; atlas, dune, and bridge are labels, not proofs of trust.
